description: Mulligatawny Spiced Lentil Soup is a classic Indian-inspired creation, blending creamy lentils with a symphony of aromatic spices, vegetables, and often a touch of tanginess. This hearty and comforting soup offers a delightful balance of savory, spicy, and slightly sweet notes, making it a perfect meal for a chilly evening or a wholesome lunch. Enjoy this flavorful journey into the heart of Indian culinary tradition with every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Chop the onion, mince garlic, grate ginger, dice carrot, and peel and dice the apple as specified. Have all your spices measured and ready.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat ghee or cooking oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Vegetables
instructions.text: Stir in the curry powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and release their aroma. Add the diced carrot and apple, stirring to coat them with the spices. Cook for 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Simmer the Lentils
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Finish with Coconut Milk
instructions.text: Once the lentils are tender, pour in the full-fat coconut milk. Stir well to combine. If you prefer a smoother soup, you can partially blend a portion of the soup using an immersion blender or by carefully transferring some to a regular blender, then returning it to the pot.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in the fresh lime or lemon juice just before serving. Garnish each bowl generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with a side of rice or crusty bread.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a small 'tadka' (tempering) of mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil at the very end, poured over the finished soup.
Adjust the consistency of the soup by adding more vegetable broth if you prefer a thinner consistency. For a thicker soup, simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes.
Leftover Mulligatawny soup stores beautifully in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
